foundations-01.topics: Statistical experiments, models and identifiability; estimators and randomization; losses, risks and decision theory; domination, likelihoods, sufficiency, completeness, exponential families, and exact inference.

foundations-02.topics: Point estimation and finite-sample optimality; unbiasedness, Rao–Blackwell and Lehmann–Scheffé; information bounds and their regularity; testing, Neyman–Pearson, uniformly most powerful tests, confidence sets, pivots, and inversion.

foundations-03.topics: Asymptotic inference; consistency, M/Z estimators, delta method, asymptotic normality, likelihood theory, local asymptotic normality, contiguity, asymptotic efficiency, and boundary or misspecification failures.

foundations-04.topics: Concentration inequalities and empirical processes; symmetrization, entropy and covering, chaining, uniform laws and central limit results; minimax lower bounds and decision-theoretic upper bounds, including high-dimensional foundations.

foundations-05.topics: Nonparametric and semiparametric inference; density and regression estimation, kernels and splines, approximation rates, tangent spaces, influence functions, efficient scores, semiparametric efficiency; rigorous local prerequisite map.

foundations-06.topics: Robust and high-dimensional statistical foundations; contamination, influence and breakdown, robust means, heavy tails, sparsity, covariance estimation, minimax rates; general randomized/sequential inference foundations without machine-learning dependencies.

models-01.topics: Regression and generalized linear models; likelihood theory applications, multivariate models, covariance/PCA classical inference, prediction, diagnostics, hierarchy, mixed effects and longitudinal models. Exclude Bayesian/computational prerequisites from future categories.

models-02.topics: Sampling and survey inference; inclusion probabilities, Horvitz–Thompson and variance estimates, stratification/clustering, finite populations; experimental design, blocking/factorials/aliasing, optimal design, power and sample-size methods; technical versus biological replication.

models-03.topics: Causal inference; potential outcomes and structural causal models, DAG identification, adjustment, interventions, instrumental variables, mediation and interference; missing-data mechanisms, identifiability, weighting and sensitivity; measurement-error models.

models-04.topics: Survival, reliability and event-time inference, censoring/truncation, counting-process methods, Kaplan–Meier, hazards/Cox, competing risks; scientific measurement/calibration, detection/quantification limits, agreement, batch effects and uncertainty.

models-05.topics: Time series, stationary/dependent data, autocovariance/spectral inference, ARMA, prediction and state-space definitions; spatial statistics/random fields, covariance/variograms/kriging; statistical point processes. Computational filtering goes in future category 3.

models-06.topics: Multiple testing, familywise/FDR control, simultaneous and selective inference, reproducibility; sequential tests, martingale confidence sequences, optional stopping, group-sequential and basic adaptive experiments; learning/bandit allocation reserved for future category 4.
